A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterMask research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original InterHuman and InterX evaluations, component ablations, reaction-generation results, and a user study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds masking-probability sensitivity results and expanded qualitative ablations.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE, collaborative Inter-M transformer, attention components, two-stage masking, objectives, and inference procedures remain unchanged. The additional architecture explanations and disclosure of the masking probability document the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover InterHuman and InterX interaction generation and reaction generation with and without text. The added sensitivity study and dancing ablation examples remain within the existing tasks and motion domains.

E2.justification: External baselines in Table 1 and quantitative ablation comparators in Table 3 are unchanged. However, the qualitative attention comparison expands from the no-spatio-temporal-attention variant in v1 Figure 7 to also include no-cross-attention and no-self-attention variants in v3 Figure 12.

E3.justification: v3 Table 4 introduces a controlled sweep of masking probability p_r over 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9 for interaction and reaction generation. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets, and inference settings remain unchanged. The newly stated user-study participant count documents an existing study.

E4.justification: v3 adds sensitivity analysis of the interaction-versus-reaction tradeoff across masking probabilities. Appendix H also expands qualitative attention ablations to cross-attention, self-attention, and synchronized dancing. The existing quantitative ablations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 evaluation repetitions, five for MModality, and 95% confidence intervals. Reporting for retained results is unchanged; the new masking sweep supplies point estimates without introducing another uncertainty or significance procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, user-study scores, and the main reaction-generation results are unchanged. New Table 4 reports interaction FIDs of 5.214 and 5.152 and reaction FIDs of 2.850 and 3.368 for p_r=0.7 and 0.9, respectively. Figure 12 adds qualitative ablation outcomes. These are additional settings and findings, not improved same-setting benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The geometric-loss equations move from the main text to Appendix C without substantive revision. Appendix B explicitly writes nearest-codeword quantization already described in v1; it adds no new mathematical reasoning, assumption, or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: collaborative masked interaction generation with 2D motion tokens, state-of-the-art benchmark performance, and reaction generation without task-specific redesign or fine-tuning. Their headline numerical claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D interprets p_r=0.8 as balancing interaction and reaction performance. Appendix H adds explanations linking cross-attention to reaction timing and self-attention to motion refinement, extending the earlier discussion of spatial coordination. Existing penetration, dataset-bias, and sequence-length limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies p_r=0.8, discloses 16 user-study participants, and details the VQ-VAE block arrangement and dropout. It also supplies an explicit code-repository link and states public code/checkpoint release. These supplement the substantial implementation information already present in v1.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, and the related-work discussion retains the same comparisons and research positioning. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted language and affiliation edits, adds a reproducibility statement and appendix explanations, and moves geometric-loss details and qualitative ablation discussion into appendices. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds VQ-VAE and masking diagrams in Figures 7–8 and the sensitivity table, expands the attention-ablation display into Figure 12, and relocates qualitative ablation figures to the appendix. Other figures and tables largely retain their designs, with resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The masking sweep supports a previously undocumented parameter choice, while clearer architecture diagrams, the participant count, and explicit code-access information improve transparency and reproducibility. Expanded qualitative ablations clarify component roles without losing the original evidence or limitations. These are limited gains; the central results remain unchanged and the new sensitivity table lacks uncertainty estimates.
